items.title: Everyone Uses AI Agents. So Where Are the Agent Builders?
items.summary: Lots of companies say they have AI agents in production. Far fewer seem to have built their own, and almost nobody wants to admit it's really hard. This conversation pulls apart what "agents in production" actually means, with both speakers drawing on their own work: one is hosting a virtual conference for the third time, the other is prepping a livestream for AgentCon and MCPCon in San Jose. Their case: plenty of agents already do real work. They're just Claude Code and Codex, not homegrown platforms, and nobody earns brownie points for saying so. From there it gets practical: why the agent push comes from boardrooms rather than problems, a manager's four levels of delegation applied to agents, a personal agent that follows up well but still misses context, a local "librarian" built on 7,000+ Slack DMs, what Gartner's 70% headline really says, and an AI code review loop that never called the code good enough. Are you building your own agents, or getting your value from someone else's? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more. items.title: Meet the Startup: Aegiq, A Full-Stack Photonic Quantum Computing Company
items.summary: Quantum computers have a deployment problem. Aegiq is solving it. The Sheffield-based startup is building photonic quantum computers designed to connect over standard fiber networks and manufacture using standard semiconductor processes — making quantum hardware practical to deploy at scale, not just in a lab. In this interview, Aegiq’s team walks through how they’ve integrated NVIDIA technology into their core workflow. Using NVIDIA’s Ising solver, they cut quantum dot calibration time by 3x. With cuTENSOR libraries, they went from 1 million point meshes on existing GPUs to billions — and are targeting 10 trillion point meshes in collaboration with NVIDIA. The applications are real and near-term: aerospace simulation, fusion energy, materials science, quantum chemistry. Aegiq joined NVIDIA Inception to accelerate access to customers and compute, and is now one of the startups demonstrating what happens when photonic quantum hardware meets GPU-accelerated simulation. 🌱 Aegiq is a member of NVIDIA Inception, a program supporting startups building at the frontier of AI and deep tech. Learn more about NVIDIA Inception: https://nvda.ws/4kjJM2n. #Aegiq #NVIDIAInception #QuantumComputing #AIStartups #Photonicquantum

items.title: The GCC Paradox: Why Indian IT Firms Are Helping Clients Leave Them
items.summary: India's Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem is undergoing a massive shift. What were once simple offshore back-offices focused on cost-cutting are now taking direct ownership of core product development, engineering, and AI. This transition is actively changing the relationship between multinational enterprises and traditional Indian IT services firms. In a surprising twist, IT giants are doubling down on this trend rather than fighting it. LTM recently launched "GCC Origin" to help enterprises build and run their own India hubs, while HCLTech introduced a "Nano GCC" model on AWS for smaller, AI-focused teams.
